docs.title: RHOSO 18.x operating procedures
docs.text:
Controlled-document status: DRAFT / NO-GO

The website is a public engineering reference. The SOPs have not been validated against a target RHOSO deployment or signed by an authorized approver. Do not treat them as production-approved procedures.

L1/L2/L3 start here · Production release gate · Compatibility register

docs.title: Corporate-style controlled SOP catalogue
docs.text:
The four SOPs now follow the same nine-section document layout as the supplied corporate example: document information, formal review and approval, revision history, table of contents, purpose, scope, applicability, terms and definitions, roles and responsibilities, implementation, review requirements, references, and appendices.

Area Procedure Worked example Approval Operations RHOSO-ITD-SOP-OPS-001 Daily health Example DRAFT Incidents RHOSO-ITD-SOP-INC-001 VM BUILD/ERROR Example DRAFT Maintenance RHOSO-ITD-SOP-MNT-001 Compute host Example DRAFT Recovery RHOSO-ITD-SOP-REC-001 Backup readiness Example DRAFT

Print: Open an SOP in the MkDocs site and use the browser's Print → Save as PDF function. The SOP-only A4 stylesheet applies formal header, dark section bands, grey table headers and clear revision/approval details. Browser printing does not insert or validate legal signatures or formal document-control approval.

Branding: The header uses a text-only RHOSO identifier. Replace or supplement it with an approved corporate logo only after the organization grants the appropriate rights. Do not copy the CBUAE logo, confidential legal notice, or organization name from an example.

docs.title: Updating or adding an SOP
docs.text:
1. Copy TEMPLATE.md for a new SOP or edit the appropriate existing Markdown on a Git branch.
  2. Fill in actual owner, document reference, revision, release applicability, department and approval details; do not invent signatures or dates. Keep as DRAFT until verified.
  3. Populate all nine numbered sections, with commands and expected outcomes in Section 6. Separate [OCP], [OS], [POD] and [EDPM] execution contexts, L1 read-only versus L2/L3 approved actions.
  4. Update the linked worked example where necessary; mark fictional outputs SIMULATED.
  5. Update CHANGELOG.md, catalogue and mkdocs.yml navigation if creating a new SOP; submit a PR and pass automated checks.
  6. Merge to publish the website. Actual production approval remains a separate release-gate process, not a GitHub merge.

The Markdown SOPs are the only source of truth. No duplicate Word files or independently maintained HTML viewers are required.

docs.title: SOP document control, contribution and approval
docs.text: All production-facing SOPs use the corporate nine-section format in TEMPLATE.md. The MkDocs website is generated from each Markdown SOP; there is no separately maintained Word or HTML version.

docs.title: Authoring procedure
docs.text:
1. Create a branch from main. Edit the appropriate SOP Markdown under SOP/operations/, SOP/incidents/, SOP/maintenance/, or SOP/recovery/.
  2. Update its document header/reference, revision number, developer/owner, document-control metadata, review and approval placeholders, revision table, and nine sections. Never fabricate signatures, approval dates or effective dates.
  3. Section 6 must provide ordered implementation steps, explicit context ([OCP], [OS], [EDPM], [POD]), level (L1/L2/L3), commands, expected results, interpretation/stop condition, validation, rollback and escalation. Preserve actual transaction evidence, not guesses.
  4. Confirm RHOSO/OpenShift minor and micro-release, CLI availability and deployed CRD/operator ownership against authoritative documentation. Distinguish PROVEN HEALTHY, PROVEN BROKEN, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS and UNKNOWN.
  5. Confirm approved reconciler/source of truth, impact, change approval, rollback and the original-transaction test before any write action. Do not recommend restarts, deletion, migration or restoration speculatively.
  6. Keep each category's worked example consistent. Mark all imaginary incidents, outputs and results SIMULATED.
  7. Update CHANGELOG.md, the relevant catalogue links, and MkDocs navigation for newly added SOPs.
  8. Open a pull request and require human technical review plus passing MkDocs and structure checks. The controlled version remains DRAFT until release gate is signed off.

docs.title: Publication restrictions
docs.text:
The GitHub Pages site is a public website. Use public-safe wording and placeholders. Do not paste a regulated institution's confidential legal notice, internal IPs, private keys, tenant details, incident logs or customer information into the public repository. A confidential formally issued version must be hosted in the organization's approved restricted document-management system.

The document's signature fields are intentionally blank. No Git merge or site build constitutes written authorization or proves live-cluster command safety.

docs.title: Verification from repository root
docs.text:
bash -n scripts/rhoso-healthcheck.sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs build --strict --clean
git diff --check

For visual review, run mkdocs serve; inspect the incident SOP at desktop and mobile widths and use Print → Save as PDF to verify A4 page layout. CI tests markup and presence of sections but does not certify print rendering, live RHOSO behavior, or actual approvals.

docs.title: How to submit an improvement
docs.text:
Open a GitHub issue or PR and supply: - Observed gap: which exact operational transaction failed or what manual work is error-prone. - Environment: RHOSO/OpenShift/EDPM version, feature flags, and relevant topology without secrets. - Evidence: first proven failure with timestamp and request ID, or a reasoned improvement proposal. - Recommendation: minimum technical/documentation change, source of truth and owner. - Safety: blast radius, alternatives, rollback and validation of the original transaction. - Status: PROPOSED -> IN REVIEW -> VERIFIED -> COMPLETED (or REJECTED).

Do not mark a proposal COMPLETED merely because a command was added; acceptance must be reviewed and verified.

docs.title: RHOSO SOP production release gate
docs.text:
CURRENT DECISION: NO-GO for production-authoritative L1 use

Repository CI verifies documentation and mocked script behavior, not live RHOSO compatibility, authenticating services, correct CLI privileges, or end-to-end tenant transactions. The four existing SOPs remain DRAFT.

docs.title: Release criteria (must all be complete)
docs.text:
• [ ] Named owner and approver for each production-approved SOP; support team and review date.
  • [ ] Exact RHOSO micro-release / OpenShift / EDPM / Ceph / enabled services, documented in compatibility.
  • [ ] Commands reviewed against installed CLI/plugins/CRDs with actual namespace, pod and container discovery; uncertain commands labeled UNVERIFIED.
  • [ ] L1 read-only steps and L2/L3 approved changes separated and reviewed.
  • [ ] Production maintenance changes have authoritative Operator/GitOps/Helm ownership, impact, stop conditions and tested rollback.
  • [ ] Incidents trace the original transaction with matching request ID/time; validation reproduces it.
  • [ ] Daily health-check is tested against controlled healthy/degraded/unavailable fixtures and observed on a permitted RHOSO test environment.
  • [ ] Critical incident SOPs cover Nova/Placement, compute registration, OVN/Neutron, Cinder/Ceph, RabbitMQ, Galera and RHOSO Operators; no fabricated runbook claims.
  • [ ] Backup evidence includes supported, isolated restore exercise and RPO/RTO sign-off for actual backends.
  • [ ] Required PR review, CI and branch protection are configured and independently verified.
  • [ ] The live Pages URL is accessible from engineer networks; navigation/search/browser/print checks pass.
  • [ ] L1/L2/L3 training and escalation simulation completed with documented feedback.

docs.title: Engineer start here — RHOSO operational boundaries
docs.text:
Production release status: HOLD

These SOPs are DRAFT until the release gate is signed off against the target RHOSO deployment. L1 engineers must not execute [CHANGE], [DELETE] or unverified commands.

docs.title: First five minutes of an incident
docs.text:
1. Capture the exact failing tenant/system transaction, region, UTC incident time, VM/resource/request ID and customer-visible symptom.
  2. Identify current versus incident-time state, and first evidence-supported failing service boundary.
  3. Run the read-only discovery commands in the matching SOP using its indicated [OCP]/[OS]/[EDPM]/[POD]/[CEPH] context.
  4. Record PROVEN HEALTHY, PROVEN BROKEN, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, UNKNOWN; avoid assigning root cause without proof.
  5. Redact evidence, open ticket, and hand off with a clearly named owner and missing evidence.
Role Authorized use of these DRAFT references Stop/escalation L1 Identity/scope, resource status, logs and read-only API calls subject to approved RBAC Any state-changing action, unclear scope, credential access, or cross-domain failure → L2 L2 Service-specific RCA and change proposal; execute only separately approved release-verified SOP Changes affecting cells, production VMs, networking, databases or storage with missing rollback → L3 L3 / Architect Cross-domain design and risk assessment, approved changes, DR planning and escalation to Red Hat Any unsupported release, unclear authoritative owner, data-loss possibility → stop/change authority

docs.title: Incident escalation bundle
docs.text: Required item Evidence User transaction Command/API/user workflow, input scope, expected outcome, observed error Correlation UTC time, region, request ID, VM/port/volume/host reference (secure ticket only) First failure Short, timestamped, redacted log or API response and generating component Proven healthy/broken Stage-by-stage validated boundary; unrelated layers excluded Unknown Specific missing test, unavailable API or permission Ownership Operator CR/GitOps/Helm authority and owning team Action status Read-only investigation, proposed change, approval ID, rollback, original-transaction validation

docs.title: TABLE OF CONTENTS
docs.text: Section Content Section Content 1 Purpose 6 Implementation 2 Scope 7 Review requirements 3 Applicability 8 References 4 Terms & definitions 9 Appendices 5 Roles & responsibilities

docs.title: 1 PURPOSE
docs.text:
Trace the specific instance-create transaction from API acceptance through scheduling, resource claims, networking and guest boot. BUILD/ERROR is a symptom, not root-cause evidence.

Acceptance: Identify the earliest error correlated to the same instance/request ID and UTC incident time. Remediation is in a separately approved fault-domain procedure; validate by reproducing the original server-create transaction.

docs.title: 2 SCOPE
docs.text:
Use OpenStack API and discovered RHOSO/EDPM service logs. Scope to the affected region, project, Nova cell and workload. Optional storage or networking services are investigated only where the transaction implicates them.

  • [OCP] authenticated OpenShift administration workstation.
  • [OS] authenticated, discovered OpenStackClient pod.
  • [EDPM] approved RHEL data-plane host.
  • [POD] discovered container in its actual namespace.

docs.title: 3 APPLICABILITY
docs.text:
Applies to authorized operations and incident responders at L1, L2 and L3 for production, staging, UAT and DR where a supported RHOSO 18.x deployment is documented. L1 performs evidence collection only; any modification requires a separately approved change.

Document usage: Incident / read-only investigation. The procedure's read-only versus change-controlled boundaries are normative; a merged documentation change does not authorize infrastructure modifications.

docs.title: 4 TERMS & DEFINITIONS
docs.text: No. Term Description 1 RHOSO Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift. 2 Nova OpenStack Compute service managing instance creation and lifecycle. 3 Placement OpenStack resource inventories, allocation and candidate selection service. 4 EDPM External Data Plane Management for RHOSO compute and data-plane services. 5 Instance UUID / Request ID Identifiers used to correlate a specific VM and its associated API/service transaction. 6 BUILD / ERROR Instance lifecycle states indicating provisioning is in progress or has failed; neither proves root cause.

docs.title: 5 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
docs.text: No. Responsible party Role and responsibilities 1 Requesting / Application Team Report failed instance, project, region, UTC timestamp, user-visible error and business impact. 2 L1 Operations Confirm scope and ticket, collect read-only VM/events/status evidence, escalate without guessing the failing component. 3 L2 RHOSO Platform Correlate Nova scheduler/conductor and implicated service evidence; establish first proven failing hop. 4 L3 / Architect / Change Authority Review cross-domain cause, authoritative controllers, mitigation/rollback and approval of any mutating remediation.

docs.title: 6 IMPLEMENTATION
docs.text: Trace a specific server creation transaction across Nova, Placement, Neutron, Glance, Cinder and EDPM when evidence implicates those services.

docs.title: 6.1 Prerequisites and authorization
docs.text:
• Incident ticket with VM UUID, project, region, request ID (if available) and UTC time window.
  • Discover RHOSO namespace and authorized OpenStackClient pod; confirm actual containers before logs.
  • Confirm read-only access to affected Nova, Neutron and Placement APIs; document access gaps.

docs.title: 6.2 Impact, risk and stop conditions
docs.text:
STOP

No instance retry, rebuild, deletion, live migration, quota change, scheduler restart, or cell discovery based only on BUILD/ERROR. An unproven scheduler assumption must never drive a production change.

docs.title: 6.3 Decision flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
A["Record exact VM request + time"] --> B["Nova instance details and events"]
B --> C{"First matched failure?"}
C -- "No" --> D["Correlate Nova API/scheduler/conductor logs"]
C -- "Yes" --> E["Classify owning fault domain"]
D --> E
E --> F["Read-only targeted Placement/Neutron/storage/EDPM evidence"]
F --> G["Escalate minimal evidence and reproduction test"]

docs.title: 6.4 Execution procedure
docs.text:
Step 1 — Discover execution environment [OCP, read-only].

oc get openstackcontrolplanes -A
oc get pods -n "$RHOSO_NAMESPACE" -o wide
oc get pod -n "$RHOSO_NAMESPACE" "$NOVA_POD" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].name}'

Expected: real namespace, Nova scheduler/conductor/API pod name and chosen container are identified; no pod names are invented. Set RHOSO_NAMESPACE, NOVA_POD, and NOVA_CONTAINER from this discovery.

**Step 2 — Run OpenStack commands inside the discovered authenticated OpenStackClient [OS, read-only]. Use an authorized session, not the OpenShift workstation shell.

openstack token issue -f value -c expires
openstack server show "$VM_UUID" -f yaml
openstack server event list "$VM_UUID"
openstack port list --server "$VM_UUID"
openstack server volume list "$VM_UUID"

Expected: state, fault details and related resources for the same VM UUID. event list availability/visibility depends on installed client and RBAC. An API success does not prove guest boot.

Step 3 — Inspect scheduler and compute eligibility [OS, read-only].

openstack compute service list
openstack hypervisor stats show
openstack resource provider list

Expected: service state and capacity inventory. Aggregate capacity alone does not establish eligibility; compare the actual request's flavor, traits, AZ, NUMA and cell mappings.

Step 4 — Correlate logs by exact request and time [OCP, read-only].

oc logs -n "$RHOSO_NAMESPACE" "$NOVA_POD" -c "$NOVA_CONTAINER" --timestamps --since=60m

Expected: matching instance/request ID at the incident time. Set a different historical collection window if needed; absence of a matching line means UNKNOWN.

Step 5 — Only follow the first proven failing hop. If the matched failure is Neutron port binding, inspect that port and OVN binding; if Cinder mapping, inspect the specific volume transaction; if scheduling, inspect Placement allocations/inventories and Nova cell host mapping. Do not perform all tests without an evidenced need.

docs.title: 6.5 Acceptance and validation
docs.text: After separate approved remediation, reproduce the original server-create request with equivalent region, flavor, network, storage constraints and project policy. Verify ACTIVE, actual compute placement, console/guest boot, intended ports and attached volumes. Record original and new request IDs; API acceptance alone is insufficient.

docs.title: 6.6 Rollback or restoration
docs.text: Read-only SOP; none. Any proposed change must separately define authoritative owner, impact, explicit rollback steps and guest/storage consistency checks.

docs.title: 6.7 Evidence handling and escalation
docs.text:
PROVEN BROKEN: earliest correlated scheduler, port-binding, image, volume or compute error. PROVEN HEALTHY: successful prior stages matched to this request. INFERENCE: resulting inability to boot. HYPOTHESIS: NoValidHost caused by quota/traits/host capacity (unproven without inventories). UNKNOWN: missing logs, project visibility, or request ID.

Use L1–L3 ownership and escalation. Record incident-time and current-time evidence separately. A user-facing failure is not automatically proof of the ticket's assumed fault domain.

docs.title: 7 REVIEW REQUIREMENTS
docs.text:
This SOP shall be reviewed at least annually, when the deployed RHOSO micro-release or related Operators change, and after significant incidents, topology changes, or revised security and operational policies. The document developer updates the revision record; the RHOSO technical lead and IT Operations reviewer verify commands, scope, evidence, role boundaries and applicability before the designated approver authorizes its effective date.

Prior revisions must remain recoverable through Git history or the approved document-control system. An automated MkDocs build and Git merge do not constitute authorization for production execution.

docs.title: 1 PURPOSE
docs.text: Execute approved compute maintenance without unplanned scheduling, VM migrations or loss of tenant availability. Acceptance: original workload transactions succeed after maintenance, host returns to required state, and every affected VM has an approved disposition.

docs.title: 2 SCOPE
docs.text: [OCP] inventory Operator-owned OpenStackDataPlaneNodeSet and deployments; [OS] use authenticated OpenStackClient for Nova queries; [EDPM] any host operations require separate release-supported procedure. This SOP does not authorize reboot, rebuild, fencing or Ceph work.

docs.title: 3 APPLICABILITY
docs.text:
Applies to supported compute host maintenance in production, staging, UAT and DR with an approved change ticket. L1 inventory only; scheduling changes and migrations are restricted to authorized L2/L3 engineers.

Document usage: Maintenance / approved change. The procedure's read-only versus change-controlled boundaries are normative; a merged documentation change does not authorize infrastructure modifications.

docs.title: 4 TERMS & DEFINITIONS
docs.text: No. Term Description 1 EDPM External Data Plane Management; manages RHOSO external data-plane nodes. 2 Nova Compute OpenStack service responsible for compute-host registration and VM lifecycle operations. 3 Disable scheduling Administrative action preventing new instance placement; it does not relocate existing workloads. 4 Live migration Supported movement of a running VM subject to CPU, PCI, NUMA, cell, network and storage compatibility. 5 Rollback Explicit, pre-approved procedure to return a specific change to a safe previous state.

docs.title: 5 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
docs.text: No. Responsible party Role and responsibilities 1 Change Requester Provide host scope, affected guests, business impact, maintenance window and approvals. 2 L1 Operations Discover hosts, collect read-only compute and VM inventories and document findings. 3 L2 RHOSO Engineer Execute approved scheduling and per-VM maintenance actions; monitor acceptance and stop conditions. 4 L3 / Architect / Workload Owner Verify topology, migration suitability, storage consistency, rollback and final workload validation. 5 Change Management Approve the ticket and ensure communication, evidence and closure requirements.

docs.title: 6 IMPLEMENTATION
docs.text: Maintain an identified EDPM compute host with explicit workload approvals, Nova scheduling constraints, rollback and original-transaction validation.

docs.title: 6.1 Prerequisites and authorization
docs.text:
• Named maintenance owner, ticket, approved workload list, window, communication and recovery plan.
  • Check Instance HA interaction (if deployed), Nova cell membership, AZ/aggregates and Placement traits.
  • Verify each guest's CPU compatibility, PCI/SR-IOV, NUMA/hugepages, storage and migration compatibility before considering live migration.
  • Verify target host headroom for the actual flavor and constraints, not aggregate vCPU/RAM only.
  • Determine CR/GitOps/Helm authoritative configuration ownership before any changes.

docs.title: 6.2 Impact, risk and stop conditions
docs.text:
STOP

Never disable or migrate a host until workload owner approval, supported migration method, target eligibility and rollback are documented. A scheduler-disable action does not move existing VMs. Do not perform automatic evacuation or reboot.

docs.title: 6.3 Decision flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
 A["Approved change + source host identity"] --> B["Inventory guests / constraints"]
 B --> C{"Every guest has approved disposition?"}
 C -- "No" --> STOP["STOP / escalate"]
 C -- "Yes" --> D["Confirm placement + storage/migration compatibility"]
 D --> E{"Approved destination and rollback?"}
 E -- "No" --> STOP
 E -- "Yes" --> F["Disable new scheduling under change"]
 F --> G["Only approved migrations / host work"]
 G --> H["Reproduce workload transactions"]
 H --> I["Enable scheduling only when host fit"]

docs.title: 6.4 Execution procedure
docs.text:
Step 1 — Discover management ownership [OCP, read-only].

oc get openstackdataplanenodesets -A
oc get openstackdataplanedeployments -A

Expected: exact NodeSet/deployment and authoritative controller path, not guessed names.

Step 2 — Verify compute and affected workload inventory [OS, read-only]. Supply approved COMPUTE_HOST.

openstack compute service list --host "$COMPUTE_HOST"
openstack server list --all-projects --host "$COMPUTE_HOST"
openstack hypervisor stats show

Expected: complete VM inventory and compute service state. The aggregate stats do not establish destination eligibility. Confirm Placement inventory/traits/NUMA/PCI and each VM's attached volumes.

Step 3 — L2/L3 ONLY: disable new scheduling [OS, CHANGE]. Do not execute without a documented and approved change ID.

openstack compute service set --disable --disable-reason "$CHANGE_ID" "$COMPUTE_HOST" nova-compute
openstack compute service list --host "$COMPUTE_HOST"

Expected: service disabled for new scheduling. Existing guests remain on the host. This does not validate readiness to reboot.

Step 4 — Migration execution requires a separate per-guest approved plan. Do not use a generic bulk migration or automatic host reboot. Validate migration target, availability zone, same-cell requirements, NUMA/PCI, storage, Instance HA, downtime and rollback for each VM. Use RHOSO maintenance documentation.

Step 5 — L2/L3 ONLY: enable scheduling after source host and user transactions pass [OS, CHANGE].

openstack compute service set --enable "$COMPUTE_HOST" nova-compute
openstack compute service list --host "$COMPUTE_HOST"

Expected: service up/enabled; further validation of guest placement and APIs still required.

docs.title: 6.5 Acceptance and validation
docs.text: Verify each migrated/retained guest's state, placement, network reachability, storage and expected application path. Reproduce the approved original VM/workload transaction. Record before/after evidence and unresolved constraints.

docs.title: 6.6 Rollback or restoration
docs.text: If only scheduler-disable occurred and host is demonstrably healthy, approved rollback is to re-enable scheduling using Step 5. Guest relocation, reboot, disk or infrastructure rollback is topology-dependent and must be written in the change record before maintenance. On migration error, stop subsequent migrations and preserve state for investigation.

docs.title: 6.7 Evidence handling and escalation
docs.text: PROVEN HEALTHY: exact host/guest checks. PROVEN BROKEN: failed migration or application transaction. INFERENCE: impacted capacity. HYPOTHESIS: storage/CPU mismatch until proven. UNKNOWN: unsupported relocation eligibility. L1 does not execute Step 3 or Step 5.

docs.title: 1 PURPOSE
docs.text:
Determine the observed state of a selected RHOSO cloud without modifying infrastructure. The check is a screening collector, not an end-to-end tenant transaction.

Acceptance: Timestamped PASS/WARN/FAIL/UNAVAILABLE/SKIP results with faults assigned for follow-up. Any incident is validated by reproducing its original transaction.

docs.title: 2 SCOPE
docs.text:
Cluster and RHOSO CR/API inventory only for services implemented in the chosen namespace. Optional services may legitimately be absent; do not force deployment assumptions.

  • [OCP] authenticated OpenShift administration workstation.
  • [OS] authenticated, discovered OpenStackClient pod.
  • [EDPM] approved RHEL data-plane host.
  • [POD] discovered container in its actual namespace.

docs.title: 3 APPLICABILITY
docs.text:
Applies to operations reviews in production, staging, UAT and DR only where the deployed RHOSO micro-release and API permissions have been verified. L1 may collect read-only evidence; L2/L3 own fault-domain diagnosis and separately approved changes.

Document usage: Operations / read-only. The procedure's read-only versus change-controlled boundaries are normative; a merged documentation change does not authorize infrastructure modifications.

docs.title: 4 TERMS & DEFINITIONS
docs.text: No. Term Description 1 RHOSO Red Hat OpenStack Services on OpenShift. 2 OCP OpenShift Container Platform; execution context for oc commands. 3 EDPM External Data Plane Management for RHOSO compute/data-plane nodes. 4 PASS / WARN / FAIL Outcome of a specific, defined read-only invariant, not full end-to-end application health. 5 UNAVAILABLE / SKIP An unverified check versus a nonapplicable optional check; neither is a success claim.

docs.title: 5 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
docs.text: No. Responsible party Role and responsibilities 1 L1 Operations Identify target cluster, execute permitted read-only collector, record status/timestamps, open incident on failures or unknown coverage. 2 L2 RHOSO Platform Investigate exact failing service/transaction, validate observed invariants, propose minimum evidence-based remediation. 3 L3 / Service Owner Confirm topology/version applicability; approve changes, recovery plans and cross-domain escalation. 4 IT Operations Manager Review handover completeness, exception handling and document control.

docs.title: 6 IMPLEMENTATION
docs.text: Read-only assessment of the deployed OpenShift and RHOSO environment; this procedure does not independently certify tenant applications.

docs.title: 6.1 Prerequisites and authorization
docs.text:
• Authenticate using the approved OpenShift identity provider; verify oc whoami.
  • Have oc, jq, Bash and rights to inspect RHOSO CRs; only approved pod exec for OpenStack API checks.
  • Discover the intended RHOSO namespace. If more than one control plane exists, choose one deliberately.
  • Use a private workstation with restricted local output storage.

docs.title: 6.2 Impact, risk and stop conditions
docs.text:
STOP

Do not restart pods, edit CRs, or delete local evidence. Treat UNAVAILABLE as not checked, never healthy; SKIP means no applicable installed service was detected. The collector does not certify Galera synchronization or tenant end-to-end functionality.

docs.title: 6.3 Decision flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
A["Authenticate and choose cloud"] --> B["Read-only health collector"]
B --> C{"FAIL or WARN?"}
C -- "Yes" --> D["Classify first proven boundary and escalate"]
C -- "No" --> E{"UNAVAILABLE / missing checks?"}
E -- "Yes" --> F["Record unknown coverage; assign verification"]
E -- "No" --> G["Record checks passed; synthetic tenant test separately"]

docs.title: 6.4 Execution procedure
docs.text:
Step 1 — Discover scope [OCP, read-only].

oc whoami
oc get openstackcontrolplanes -A
oc get openstackdataplanenodesets -A
oc get openstackdataplanedeployments -A

Expected: One or more real RHOSO instances are identified. STOP if the target namespace is ambiguous or inaccessible.

Step 2 — Verify and execute the read-only collector [OCP]. Run from the checked-out repository root.

bash -n scripts/rhoso-healthcheck.sh
RHOSO_NAMESPACE="<discovered-rhoso-namespace>" bash scripts/rhoso-healthcheck.sh

Expected: a timestamped, locally restricted report folder and summary. Syntax check exit 0 only proves Bash syntax.

Step 3 — Interpret each result.

Status Meaning L1 action PASS The explicitly implemented invariant passed at this time Record scope and timestamp; not E2E proof WARN Degraded, incomplete, or potential issue Open ticket with evidence and owning team FAIL A failure of a defined invariant was observed Escalate with first proven boundary UNAVAILABLE The check could not establish a state Escalate verification gap; do not assume healthy SKIP The optional check was not applicable Record absence and deployment baseline

Step 4 — Reproduce the actual reported failing transaction using a separately approved read-only API call or safe synthetic test; a green Kubernetes object is not sufficient.

docs.title: 6.5 Acceptance and validation
docs.text: Capture the report path, UTC timestamp, selected cloud namespace and any unverified checks. Confirm that any reported application problem is reproduced from the authorized client. The script is not proof of full cloud availability.

docs.title: 6.6 Rollback or restoration
docs.text: No infrastructure modification; no rollback. Follow approved local evidence retention for report files.

docs.title: 6.7 Evidence handling and escalation
docs.text:
PROVEN HEALTHY: checks with exact predicates satisfied. PROVEN BROKEN: failed predicate and timestamp. INFERENCE: possible effects on users. HYPOTHESIS: candidate cause, unproven. UNKNOWN: missing API, credentials, log or test. Provide a redacted summary rather than uploading raw output.

Use L1–L3 ownership and escalation. Record incident-time and current-time evidence separately. A user-facing failure is not automatically proof of the ticket's assumed fault domain.

This SOP shall be reviewed at least annually, when the deployed RHOSO micro-release or related Operators change, and after significant incidents, topology changes, or revised security and operational policies. docs.text:
[!WARNING] SIMULATED TRAINING EXAMPLE. All evidence below is invented to illustrate documentation technique. Do not copy identifiers, assume a diagnosis or execute change steps without site approval.

Field Value Applicable SOP SOP-REC-001 Scenario Backup readiness audit Status EXAMPLE ONLY / not approved Evidence type SIMULATED, not from a live cluster Contexts [OCP] workstation; [OS] authenticated OpenStackClient where specified Version RHOSO 18.x concept; exact micro-release unverified

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: Show an engineer how to apply the related SOP, interpret expected results, decide when to stop, and document the actual success criteria.

docs.title: 2. Scope
docs.text: Training only. No real cluster objects, pod names, credentials, IP addresses or tenant identifiers.

docs.title: 3. Preconditions
docs.text: Discover deployment, authenticate by approved method, verify installed OpenStackClient, and record incident or change ticket before action.

docs.title: 4. Impact and risks
docs.text: [!CAUTION] Do not translate fictional observations into production root-cause assertions. Mutating steps require formal change approval, ownership and documented rollback.

docs.title: 5. Decision path
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A["Locate precise scope + request"] --> B["Read-only evidence"]
  B --> C{"First proven boundary?"}
  C -- "No" --> D["UNKNOWN: collect evidence / escalate"]
  C -- "Yes" --> E["Document impact and owner"]
  E --> F["Only approved action if needed"]
  F --> G["Reproduce original transaction"]

docs.title: 6. Detailed procedure — example walkthrough
docs.text: Step What the engineer does Simulated evidence / expected output Interpretation / next action 1 Determine deployed RHOSO/OpenShift/OADP releases and compare Red Hat's release-specific support requirements. Document actual command output in secure incident ticket Follow linked SOP; stop if ambiguous 2 Run oc api-resources \| grep -Ei 'velero\|dataprotectionapplication\|volumesnapshot' to learn which backup APIs are present. Document actual command output in secure incident ticket Follow linked SOP; stop if ambiguous 3 SIMULATED example: backup CR shows completed but no evidence exists of restored Galera state or attached PVC data. This does not prove recoverability. SIMULATED sample only Do not extrapolate without live proof 4 Record backup completion separately from recovery assurance, verify artifact location/security and obtain last authorized isolated restore-exercise record. Document actual command output in secure incident ticket Follow linked SOP; stop if ambiguous 5 Declare readiness UNVERIFIED until a controlled restore actually meets RPO/RTO acceptance criteria; never run restore/destructive commands from this example. Document actual command output in secure incident ticket Follow linked SOP; stop if ambiguous

docs.title: 7. Validation
docs.text:
Declare readiness UNVERIFIED until a controlled restore actually meets RPO/RTO acceptance criteria; never run restore/destructive commands from this example.

Acceptance evidence: record exact command/transaction, timestamp, expected vs actual user-visible result, fault-domain boundary and secure redacted ticket link.

docs.title: 8. Rollback / recovery
docs.text: This example performs no live modifications. No automatic rollback is run. Approved changes must specify independent prerequisites and rollback before execution.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting and escalation
docs.text: Classify observations as PROVEN HEALTHY, PROVEN BROKEN, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS and UNKNOWN. Simulated outputs cannot prove any real fault.

docs.title: TABLE OF CONTENTS
docs.text: Section Content Section Content 1 Purpose 6 Implementation 2 Scope 7 Review requirements 3 Applicability 8 References 4 Terms & definitions 9 Appendices 5 Roles & responsibilities

docs.title: 1 PURPOSE
docs.text: Evaluate whether configured backups are recent and whether there is independent, documented restore evidence meeting the organization's RPO and RTO. A completed Velero Backup or a Bound PVC alone does not establish recovery viability.

docs.title: 2 SCOPE
docs.text: [OCP] authenticated admin workstation. OADP/Velero and VolumeSnapshot APIs are optional; inspect only if installed. External Ceph/ODF, MariaDB/Galera data and EDPM host configurations may require separately managed protection.

docs.title: 3 APPLICABILITY
docs.text:
Applies to RHOSO environments whose maintenance release and chosen OADP/Velero/storage protection methods are supported. L1 inventories read-only APIs; L2 verifies backup artifacts; the DR owner signs off restore evidence. This SOP never initiates a restore.

Document usage: Recovery / read-only audit. The procedure's read-only versus change-controlled boundaries are normative; a merged documentation change does not authorize infrastructure modifications.

docs.title: 4 TERMS & DEFINITIONS
docs.text: No. Term Description 1 RPO Recovery Point Objective; acceptable maximum data-loss window. 2 RTO Recovery Time Objective; maximum acceptable restoration duration. 3 OADP OpenShift API for Data Protection, when supported and installed. 4 Velero Kubernetes resource backup/restore tool used by applicable supported protection implementations. 5 Isolated restore test Controlled test demonstrating recovery of backed-up dependencies without impacting production.

docs.title: 5 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
docs.text: No. Responsible party Role and responsibilities 1 L1 Operations Identify release and optional backup APIs; collect authorized read-only inventory. 2 L2 Backup / Storage Team Verify reported backup status, artifact integrity, retention, encryption and data consistency. 3 L3 / DR Owner Approve isolated restore methodology and confirm RPO/RTO and recovered services. 4 Platform Owner Identify relevant RHOSO/OCP/EDPM/Ceph support matrix and dependencies.

docs.title: 6 IMPLEMENTATION
docs.text: Review compatibility, backup artifacts, retention and supported isolated restore evidence to determine whether the deployed RHOSO control plane meets documented recovery objectives.

docs.title: 6.1 Prerequisites and authorization
docs.text:
• Identify RHOSO and OpenShift exact versions, OADP/operator version and supported backup topology. The original RHOSO 18.0 OADP procedure has maintenance-release prerequisites; verify current documentation before relying on it.
  • Approved access to backup CRs without disclosing credentials.
  • Defined recovery objectives, off-cluster storage owner, last authorized isolated restore test and change authority for any eventual DR exercise.

docs.title: 6.2 Impact, risk and stop conditions
docs.text:
STOP

No restore, backup deletion, namespace replacement or storage manipulation from this page. If compatibility, artifact integrity, backup scope, or isolated restore evidence is unknown, report UNVERIFIED and escalate to the DR owner.

docs.title: 6.3 Decision flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
 A["Discover platform release + backup APIs"] --> B{"Supported method installed?"}
 B -- "No / UNKNOWN" --> C["UNAVAILABLE: contact DR owner"]
 B -- "Yes" --> D["Inspect backup and storage locations"]
 D --> E{"Recent successful artifact?"}
 E -- "No" --> C
 E -- "Yes" --> F{"Independent isolated restore evidence?"}
 F -- "No" --> G["Recovery UNVERIFIED"]
 F -- "Yes" --> H["Compare RPO/RTO and scope"]

docs.title: 6.4 Execution procedure
docs.text:
Step 1 — Inspect platform and backup API discovery [OCP, read-only].

oc whoami
oc get clusterversion
oc get openstackcontrolplanes -A
oc api-resources | grep -Ei 'velero|dataprotectionapplication|volumesnapshot'

Expected: actual compatible APIs or documented absence. grep can exit 1 if no optional resources: classify UNAVAILABLE, not an infrastructure failure.

Step 2 — If applicable CRDs exist, inspect backup resources [OCP, read-only].

oc get dataprotectionapplications.oadp.openshift.io -A
oc get backupstoragelocations.velero.io -A
oc get backups.velero.io -A
oc get schedules.velero.io -A
oc get volumesnapshots.snapshot.storage.k8s.io -A

Expected: inventory and reported phase. Execute only commands whose API exists; failures from missing optional CRDs do not imply backup failure.

Step 3 — Review recovery acceptance evidence. Obtain the actual latest artifact, retention, off-cluster access, encryption controls, database/PVC consistency guarantees and last supported isolated restore test from the authorized storage/DR owner. Do not retrieve backup data or secrets into the runbook.

docs.title: 6.5 Acceptance and validation
docs.text: Record backup age versus RPO, test restore time versus RTO, resources restored (including DB/PVC where applicable), date, storage backend and secure ticket reference. If no isolated restore passed, the result is UNVERIFIED; do not mark PASS.

docs.title: 6.6 Rollback or restoration
docs.text: Read-only; none. Actual DR restoration requires an independently approved, supported, exercised procedure including fencing and data consistency safeguards.

docs.title: 6.7 Evidence handling and escalation
docs.text: PROVEN HEALTHY: backup/storage/restore checks supported by redacted test evidence. PROVEN BROKEN: a backed-up dependency or supported restore test failed. INFERENCE: recovery impact. HYPOTHESIS: specific storage/DB cause without logs. UNKNOWN: absent test or inaccessible storage evidence. Escalate to DR/DBA/storage owners.

docs.title: 7 REVIEW REQUIREMENTS
docs.text:
This SOP shall be reviewed at least annually, when the deployed RHOSO micro-release or related Operators change, and after significant incidents, topology changes, or revised security and operational policies. The document developer updates the revision record; the RHOSO technical lead and IT Operations reviewer verify commands, scope, evidence, role boundaries and applicability before the designated approver authorizes its effective date.

Prior revisions must remain recoverable through Git history or the approved document-control system. An automated MkDocs build and Git merge do not constitute authorization for production execution.
